body: Iemhoff, Rosalie, in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry "Intuitionism in the Philosophy of Mathematics" says: "Intuitionism is a philosophy of mathematics that was introduced by the Dutch mathematician L.E.J. Brouwer (1881–1966). Intuitionism is based on the idea that mathematics is a creation of the mind. The truth of a mathematical statement can only be conceived via a mental construction that proves it to be true, and the communication between mathematicians only serves as a means to create the same mental process in different minds." This card reports that entry's preamble. It does not treat the entry as the original paper it cites.
